text:
maria: heads-up — planning a midnight egress queue reset + rolling node drains in us-east2 to apply nic microcode. window: 00:30-02:00 UTC. expected: partial capacity loss in gpu-pool-alpha. tagging SRE and support so we can coordinate rollback/backfill.

opsbot: scheduled maintenance created: MAINT-7901. Notifying customers with active reservations in us-east2.

daan: what % capacity do you estimate we'll lose? any spike to latency we should pre-announce to product?

maria: estimate ~20% available GPU throughput during peak of the drain (30–45m). latency risk mostly for long-seq requests; short text gen should be fine. plan: canary drain one rack at 00:35, validate KV cache warmup, then stagger remainder 10m apart.

kevin: FYI if we backfill with on-demand, cost may ramp a lot. can we prefer burst from dedicated pool-beta first, then fall back to spots? also suggest disabling model-burst routing for window to avoid cross-region spillover.

sre-oncall: runbook link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/nic-microcode-drain — will be oncall for the canary. I'll run the drain and watch queue_latency, token_throughput, and pod_evictions.

kevin: for safer rollback, add a lightweight fallback policy to route to smaller model variants (gpt-medium) if tail latency > 1.2s. cheaper and easier than spinning extra GPUs quickly.

maria: good call. I'll add the fallback policy to the routing config and push the canary flag.

sre-oncall: cordon + drain command I plan to use for the canary (single node):

```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-az2-rack3-07
kubectl drain gpu-node-az2-rack3-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
I'll also pre-warm pool-beta with 2 warm instances from dedicated capacity 15m before the canary.

daan: can you post expected customer impact message for CS? they asked for wording earlier.

maria: draft for CS: "We will perform a scheduled maintenance in us-east2 on <date> 00:30–02:00 UTC. You may see transient capacity reduction and slightly increased latency for long-sequence workloads. No persistent data loss is expected. We will route traffic to fallback variants if latency exceeds thresholds."

opsbot: notification sent to #customer-notices and updated status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/MAINT-7901

kevin: also added a quick cost-estimate: expected 4–6h of warm backfill across pools at ~+$1200 USD in worst case if spots don't fill. we can absorb but want to call it out to finance.

maria: noted — looping finance.

sre-oncall: I'll create the canary monitor: alert if queue_latency_p50 > 800ms or queue_latency_p95 > 1200ms or error_rate > 0.5% during the window. If triggered, abort further drains and uncordon last node.

maria: task list: (1) kevin toggle model-burst routing and add fallback variant; (2) sre-oncall run canary and monitors; (3) opsbot send customer notice (done); (4) me oversee warmup/backfill and finalize rollback.

maria: thanks team — will post updates in this thread as we go. :thumbsup:
